verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim documents the core workflow this story asks for: importing robots and scenes from URDF, MJCF, CAD, or USD, then simulating them with PhysX or Newton physics and RTX/physics-based sensors. Scenes are assembled by assigning materials, enabling physics, and configuring robot and sensor models, and robots can be tuned for physics accuracy before software- or hardware-in-the-loop testing. One developer reports sim-to-real drift from GPU execution-order nondeterminism in complex scenes; this is a fidelity caveat, not a refutation of the capability. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of physics and sensor realism, detailed evidence on sensor noise and fidelity modeling, and answers to the reported sim-to-real drift in complex contact scenarios.
